learning_objective: The learner will judge whether the verb in each of ten outcome statements is measurable, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** outcome-verb-checker
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether the verb in each of ten outcome statements is measurable, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Learning Outcome, Learning Objective, Measurable Verb (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each statement the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the test question is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) "Understand" is measurable because teachers use it all the time. (2) A longer statement is more measurable. (3) A measurable verb makes an outcome a good one. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging a verb against the test "could I observe this?" is an Evaluate-level action. Ten statements that mix vague and measurable verbs in similar sentences make the learner apply the test to the verb itself and not to the topic. **Content:** The test, shown at all times: could a teacher watch a learner do this and tell whether it happened? The two bins: Measurable, and Not measurable. The ten statements: | # | Statement shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | Better wording (for Not measurable) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Students will understand the water cycle. | Not measurable | "Understand" cannot be observed. | Students will explain the water cycle in four steps. | | 2 | Students will list the four main stages of the water cycle. | Measurable | A list can be seen and checked. | Not needed. | | 3 | Students will know the parts of a cell. | Not measurable | "Know" cannot be observed. | Students will label the parts of a cell on a diagram. | | 4 | Students will calculate the area of a rectangle from its length and width. | Measurable | A calculation produces a result that can be checked. | Not needed. | | 5 | Students will appreciate the importance of clean water. | Not measurable | "Appreciate" is a feeling that cannot be observed directly. | Students will describe two ways clean water affects health. | | 6 | Students will compare a primary source and a secondary source. | Measurable | A comparison can be written or spoken and then checked. | Not needed. | | 7 | Students will learn about fractions. | Not measurable | "Learn about" names no action. | Students will add two fractions with like denominators. | | 8 | Students will design a fair test to compare two fertilizers. | Measurable | A design is a product that can be reviewed. | Not needed. | | 9 | Students will be familiar with the causes of the war. | Not measurable | "Be familiar with" cannot be observed. | Students will name three causes of the war and explain one. | | 10 | Students will judge which of two websites is more reliable and give two reasons. | Measurable | The judgment and the reasons can be checked. | Not needed. | **Provenance:** The statements are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The list of measurable and vague verbs follows the chapter section "Measurable Verb". **Rules:** Each statement has exactly one correct bin, five per bin. A statement is Measurable when its main verb names an observable action. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one statement and the two bins. 2. The learner places the statement in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. For a Not measurable statement the sim also shows the better wording. 5. After statement 10 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 statements in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 9 or more it adds "You can spot a vague verb." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed statement. **Starting State:** The first statement, the test question, and two empty bins. The question shown is "Could a teacher observe this?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says know, understand, learn, appreciate, and be familiar with are not measurable, and that list, describe, calculate, compare, and design are measurable.
